key_insight: Using inpatient EMR data and clinician-prioritized variables, the study could predict 30-day heart failure readmission only modestly well.
clinical_relevance: The findings suggest readmission risk tools may work better if hospitals reliably capture clinically important variables during routine care.
method: Modified Delphi process selected candidate predictors
Natural language processing extracted variables from clinical notes and other EMR fields
Competing-risk survival models predicted 30-, 90-, and 365-day readmission
evidence_signal: In 15,160 heart failure admissions from Calgary (2011-2019), the final 30-day readmission model achieved a C-statistic of 64.4.
watch_item: Several variables thought to matter were not recorded reliably enough for modeling, which limits performance and real-world deployment.
paper_title: Developing a Heart Failure Readmission Model From Inpatient Electronic Medical Record Data
